observable_outcome: One Repository and one Increment run end to end through the real claude CLI on this machine, metered by a fail-closed cost ledger that refuses to spawn a process unless an approved provider preflight record admits it; the run's Increment Artifact, crash resume, real error and real cancellation are each proven by a named invocation; the CLI's identity (absolute path, version 2.1.241, resolved argv, session_id, usage, cost, duration) is recorded in evidence while no prompt and no response text is; and credential material is shown never to enter the Control Plane, the Work Packet, the bounded log, the canonical state or the argv, because the Secret Broker hands the claude CLI nothing at all.

acceptance_criteria: B0. V2-047 has merged into v2 before any work starts here: contracts/schemas/provider-preflight.json, internal/contracts.CheckProviderPreflightLedger and the representative_provider declaration all exist at HEAD. If any is missing, stop and escalate; do not add them here (contracts/** and internal/contracts/** are prohibited).

B1. .agents/v2/provider-preflight/V2-017-provider-live-claude.json exists, validates against contracts/schemas/provider-preflight.json, and declares provider {name: claude, version: 2.1.241, executable_path: /home/takushi/.local/bin/claude}, limits {max_invocations: 16, max_total_cost_usd: 10.00, worst_case_reservation_usd: 1.00, currency: USD, window: total, fail_closed: true, ledger_path: /home/takushi/.local/state/agentic-loop/v2/V2-017-provider-cost.json, enforced_by naming internal/runner.SupervisedInvocationRunner and internal/runner.CostLedger}, environment {granted_names: [], base_names: the justified minimum}, and an approval block whose approver, approved_at and approval_reference were supplied by the human owner, with subject_path .agents/v2/packets/V2-017-work-order.json and subject_digest equal to that file's sha256. Verify: devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -v -run TestProviderPreflightLedger ./internal/contracts.

B2. internal/runner/costledger.go defines CostLedger with Reserve, TrueUp and Snapshot implementing dp-v2-017 d2 and d4: file at the record's absolute ledger_path, 0600 in a 0700 directory, temp-file + fsync + rename on every mutation, preflight_digest re-verified on every Reserve, entries carrying sequence/purpose/state/reserved_usd/actual_usd/session_id/started_at/finished_at, and a persistent halted flag.

B3. Each of the nine refusal cases of dp-v2-017 d3 has its own negative test in internal/runner/costledger_test.go, and each asserts that NO process was started (not merely that an error was returned). Verify: devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -v -run 'TestCostLedger|TestSupervisedInvocationRunnerFailsClosed' ./internal/runner.

B4. A zero-value SupervisedInvocationRunner{} returns an error and starts nothing, and there is no exported constructor or field combination that lets a caller spawn without a CostLedger and an approved record. Assert this by test, and assert by AST scan that ProcessSupervisor is referenced from exactly one non-test location in the provider execution path.

B5. TrueUp is proven to lower and never raise: a settled entry whose actual_usd is below its reserved_usd frees budget, and an attempt to true up above the reservation is rejected. An actual_usd above 2.00 sets halted:true and makes every later Reserve fail, asserted by a test that reopens the file from disk (not from memory).

B6. ProcessSupervisor gains only additive Stdin []byte and Stdout io.Writer fields; Run's signature and the TERM-then-KILL group logic are unchanged and TestSupervisorCancelsProcessGroupTERMThenKILL passes unmodified. Verify: devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -race ./internal/runner.

B7. SupervisedInvocationRunner projects the real CLI JSON per dp-v2-017 d5 and hands only the projection to Adapter.Parse. Prove with a unit test driven by a captured real response shape (fields total_cost_usd, usage, session_id, duration_api_ms, duration_ms, num_turns, is_error, type, subtype, result, uuid) that (a) handing that JSON straight to provider.ClaudeAdapter.Parse returns ErrInvalidFixture, and (b) the projection Parses successfully with a non-empty OutputDigest. (a) is the positive control that the projection is doing real work.

B8. A test asserts that neither the journal file nor any committed artefact ever contains the model's response text: search the journal bytes for a marker string that appears in the response and require its absence, while requiring the response's sha256 to be present. This must run in the live suite, against a real response.

B9. argv[0] resolution per dp-v2-017 d6: the executed argv[0] is the record's absolute executable_path, filepath.Base of it equals the adapter's argv[0], and a record whose basename differs is refused with no process started.

B10. Live suite gating per dp-v2-017 d11: every live test skips unless AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_PROVIDER=1 AND the approved record validates AND the ledger path is writable, and a skip logs with t.Logf which condition failed. Assert that devbox run --pure -- make check completes with zero live invocations by comparing the ledger's entry count before and after; record both counts.

B11. Invocation I1 (happy, journey): with the real CLI, requirement intake through claim, workspace create, Work Packet build and Validate, real invocation, checkpoint, AcceptResult, terminal ExecutionSucceeded and a non-empty Increment Artifact digest. Proves M3 completion condition 1.

B12. Invocation I2 (happy, identity and wire): the resolved absolute argv runs the real binary, the real JSON is projected and Parsed, and session_id, usage (in/out/cache-read/cache-creation counts), total_cost_usd, duration_api_ms, duration_ms and num_turns are captured into the ledger and into the evidence check summary. Also records the empirically determined minimum environment.base_names, one justification per entry. Proves M3 completion condition 3 together with B11.

B13. Invocation I3 (happy, credential isolation): all six sub-proofs of dp-v2-017 d8 (a) through (f) hold against a real invocation. Report each separately; a single combined assertion is not acceptable. Proves M3 completion condition 4.

B14. Invocation I4 (happy, lease continuity): a second Increment on the same Repository spanning more than one LeaseTTL of LeaseKeeper ticks with a real invocation in between; every RenewResponse.ExpiresAt strictly advances and the checkpoint is preserved across the renewal.

B15. Invocations I5 and I6 (crash resume, case A): I5 is SIGKILLed at the process-group level mid-invocation before any result is journaled; the resumed Execution (I6) has a different ExecutionID, a strictly greater fencing token, re-runs the provider exactly once, and the crashed attempt's late AcceptResult is rejected with domain.ErrLeaseExpired verified by errors.Is. Case B (crash after journaling) reuses I1's journaled projection and must consume zero additional invocations, asserted by a call counter reading zero. Proves M3 completion condition 2.

B16. Invocation I7 (real error): a real CLI failure induced without an API call by pointing the CLI at an unreachable base URL; the failure is classified through the adapter, the bounded log records a redacted diagnostic, the Execution ends failed, and no retry converts it to green. The evidence must state explicitly that this exercises transport failure and not model failure, and that per-Provider success/error/quota/cancel coverage remains M6's V2-028.

B17. Invocation I8 (real cancel): context cancellation during a real invocation; the process group receives TERM then KILL, the classification is FailureCancelled, no result is journaled, and the ledger entry remains reserved at worst case. Assert the child process is actually gone by polling for its absence with a bounded deadline, never with a fixed sleep.

B18. The ledger's final Snapshot shows total invocations <= 16 and settled + outstanding <= 10.00 USD, and the evidence records the full per-entry table (sequence, purpose, state, reserved, actual, session, timestamps). Every entry maps to exactly one of I1..I8 or to a named retry of one of them; an entry that cannot be mapped is a finding to escalate, not to explain away.

B19. Capacity exhaustion handling per dp-v2-017 d10 is exercised, not just implemented: with a scratch ledger pre-loaded near the ceiling, assert that the next Reserve refuses, that no process starts, and that the code path produces the capacity-exhaustion error rather than a success or a retry.

B20. Evidence record .agents/v2/evidence/V2-017-provider-live-claude.json exists with id ev-v2-017-provider-live-claude, task_id V2-017, component provider-live-claude, one checks[] entry per acceptance criterion and per invocation, observed_at set strictly later than the record's approval.approved_at, and artifact_refs carrying {artifact_id: provider-preflight, sha256: <digest of the approved record>}. No prompt, no Work Packet content and no response text appears anywhere in it. Verify: devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -v -run 'TestProviderPreflightLedger|TestActiveEvidenceIndex' ./internal/contracts.
B21. The record is appended as exactly ONE new entry to .agents/v2/evidence/index.json with evidence_hash equal to sha256 of the evidence file's final bytes; no other entry's bytes change.

B22. evidence_key is the runner component key read from devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys at the final tree AFTER git add and commit of every new file, because make evidence-keys enumerates component files through git ls-files and silently omits untracked additions. State in the check summary which component id the key came from.

B23. devbox run --pure -- make check is green, run AFTER committing this task's changes. Judge by the verdict lines, not by devbox run's exit code. devbox run --pure -- make secrets is green; if it reports a finding, diagnose by the reported File before concluding anything, and do not touch .gitleaks.toml (prohibited) - escalate instead.

B24. docs/operations/provider-live-claude.md documents: how to run the live suite (the exact devbox invocation with its -e list), where the ledger lives, how to read it, what the halted flag means and who may clear it, and what to do on capacity exhaustion.

B25. .agents/v2/task-state/V2-017.json is advanced with one appended transition per real status change (blocked -> queued -> running -> complete or failed), contiguous sequences, correct from_status chaining, hashes matching their refs, and the top-level projection of the last transition. Verify: devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -run TestCanonicalTaskStateInvariants ./internal/contracts.
constraints: Never spawn the claude CLI without first completing a successful CostLedger.Reserve against the approved record. If the ledger cannot be read, cannot be parsed, is halted, or does not admit the reservation, spawn nothing.

Hard ceiling: 16 real invocations and 10.00 USD cumulative for this task. Reaching either is a capacity-exhaustion stop, never a success. Do not raise a ceiling, do not edit the approved record's limits, and do not start a fresh ledger file to reset the count.
If any single settled invocation exceeds 2.00 USD, stop everything immediately, set the ledger's halted flag, and escalate. Do not investigate by running another invocation.

Do not retry a red acceptance criterion until it turns green. Retries exist for re-measuring after a code fix; a criterion that fails for the same reason twice is a stop-and-escalate, per release-contract.md section 9.

Do not author, guess or backdate the approval block. approver, approved_at and approval_reference come from the human owner. If they have not been supplied, stop: there is no invocation you are allowed to make.
Do not read ~/.claude/.credentials.json, in test code or otherwise, not even to build a canary. Proving isolation by reading the secret defeats the proof.

Do not record the prompt, the Work Packet contents, or any part of the model's response text in evidence, in the journal, in canonical state or in the bounded log. Only the sha256 of the response may be persisted.

Avoid the substring 'token' in evidence summaries; write usage as in/out/cache-read/cache-creation counts. gitleaks' generic-api-key rule is keyword-triggered and .gitleaks.toml is a prohibited path here.

Do not edit internal/provider/**. If the adapter appears to need a change, that is a design finding to escalate, not a path to take: the projection in internal/runner exists precisely so internal/provider stays untouched.
Do not edit internal/contracts/** or contracts/**. The provider-preflight schema and its ledger check are V2-047's deliverables.

Another agent is concurrently editing internal/release/**, docs/preview/**, docs/stable/**, docs/operations/release-local.md and .agents/v2/evidence/**. Touch none of them beyond the single new evidence file and the single appended index entry.
Live tests must skip by default and must never run inside make check. A live test that runs unconditionally is a defect even if it passes.
Do not use fixed sleeps for process liveness or death; poll an observable condition with a bounded deadline that calls t.Fatal on timeout, as internal/runner's existing tests already do.
Do not write a passed status for a check you did not run, and do not describe a transport failure as a model failure or the representative Provider's coverage as three-Provider coverage.
Commit as checkpoints; do not push. The coordinator pushes, one checkpoint at a time.
